thread:
jess_harper: heads up — right after the Calico v3.31 rollout to west2-gpu we started seeing intermittent east-west UDP drops between training pods. p50 fine, p95/p99 tails look bad, saw sawtooth packet loss pattern. anyone else? :eyes:

deploy-bot: rollout calico/3.31 -> nodes/west2-gpu completed at 2025-11-03T14:02:10Z by ci/cni-upgrade-job-482

tarek: saw this on canary earlier today, logs had a bunch of PMTU/fragmentation warnings from kernel: "NET: mtu change caused frag needed". RDMA flows are also showing QP retries on a couple nodes.

liam_ops: quick datapoint — kubectl exec to a pod on node-a -> node-b udpiperf shows periodic 1-3% loss spikes every ~30s and RTT jitter increases. tcp flows fine.

jess_harper: exact error from dmesg on node-17: 
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: rq timeout, resetting
[ 12346.000002] NETDEV WATCHDOG: cbr0 (calico): transmit queue 0 timed out
[ 12346.000105] IPv4: skb->len < frag_threshold but DF set, dropping fragment
```

liam_ops: I ran ethtool -k on the mlx5 NICs — GSO/GRO still on. mtu on the host is 9000, pod veths are 8912. After bumping pod MTU to 8900 in a single canary namespace loss dropped to ~0.2% but latency still has spikes.

tarek: interesting — calico ipip/encap mode was changed during the upgrade (we flipped hybrid-encap in the daemonset). Encapsulation + jumbo MTU interplay might be causing added headers leading to unexpected fragmentation if ECN or DF flags are involved.

sre-ops: any chance some middlebox or host sysctl was flipped? sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward, net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing?

liam_ops: checked sysctls across nodes, all uniform. tcp_mtu_probing=0 everywhere. ip_forward=1. No recent iptables changes besides Calico ipsets.

jess_harper: can we reproduce with a minimal pod pair using udp + strace to see where ICMP frag-needed originates? If kernel does DF drop, we should get ICMP "need frag" messages.

liam_ops: repro steps I ran: 
```
# on pod-a
apt-get update && apt-get install -y iperf3
iperf3 -s -p 5201 &
# on pod-b
iperf3 -c pod-a.svc.cluster.local -u -b 1G -t 300 -p 5201
```
I also tcpdump'd and captured repeated ICMP "fragmentation needed" from node-17 egress.

tarek: quick mitigation attempt: in canary I toggled Calico's Felix config to disable encapsulation (set "encapsulation: None"), traffic returned to low loss immediately, but that breaks cross-subnet routes for some clusters — not a long-term fix for west2 since we rely on encap for multi-subnet workers.

jess_harper: rollback option — revert the calico daemonset to 3.30 on west2-gpu-only? That would be safe and buys time. Is there any reason we can't rollback?

deploy-bot: rollback job calico/3.30 -> nodes/west2-gpu queued by jess_harper at 2025-11-03T15:01:12Z

sre-ops: two operational notes before rolling back: 1) some long-running RDMA jobs already retried and failed (2 tasks), we should mark affected jobs to reschedule after rollback; 2) need to coordinate GPU capacity because reschedules will spike packing in west2.

liam_ops: also note cost/region constraint — we can't shift those GPU jobs to us-west1 because we hit our quota for P4s there and procurement takes 48-72h. So rollback is our fastest recovery path.

jess_harper: agreed. rolling back on west2 only. I'll run the rollout with surge=0 to avoid new pods on upgraded CNI.

liam_ops: after rollback we should still run a follow-up: 1) enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 briefly to see if path MTU discovery helps when encap headers present; 2) add a calico Felix rule to clamp MSS on the host for UDP to avoid DF drops; 3) file bug with Calico about how hybrid-encap and jumbo MTU interact with ECN/DF handling.

tarek: logging suggestion — add a daemonset that toggles "iproute2: ip route get" checks and scrapes dmesg for 'frag needed' to bulk-collect evidence across nodes. I'll open a short-lived job.

deploy-bot: rollback calico/3.30 -> nodes/west2-gpu started at 2025-11-03T15:06:04Z (job id 7143)

oncall-bot: alert suppressed for calico-metrics on west2 during rollback window (15:05-15:30 UTC) by jess_harper :wrench:

liam_ops: preliminary after-rollback check at 15:20: iperf UDP run now stable, ICMP frag-needed gone from node dmesg, RDMA QP retries decreased to baseline.

jess_harper: rollback complete. opening a postmortem ticket and tagging Calico maintainers. patch will be queued to test a narrower change-set (no hybrid-encap flip) before reattempt. thanks everyone for fast response :heart:

sre-ops: created internal ticket INFRA-2247 with attachments (dmesg, tcpdump pcap, iperf logs). assigning to eng-networking and cni-oncall.

jess_harper: next steps: keep west2 on 3.30 until we validate encapsulation interactions in staging with jumbo frames + RDMA. schedule re-upgrade after tests pass.

liam_ops: FYI — left a small note on cost impact: reschedules added ~2 GPU-hours of extra usage in west2, should be trivial but I'll add it to the ticket.

jess_harper: closing thread for now. ping me if the regressions reappear after the rollback.
